intro: Italy’s DSU grant pays €7,000-plus a year, waives tuition and covers meals and housing — on the same need rules as Italian students. Here is how the 2027/28 round works.
description: How the Italy DSU regional scholarship works for 2027/28: amounts, ISEE ceilings, documents and timeline.
author: NextApply Team
excerpt: Italy’s DSU grant pays €7,171-8,247 a year plus tuition waiver, meals and housing — here is how the 2027/28 round works.
content:
Italy runs one of Europe’s most generous need-based scholarship systems, and most international applicants discover it too late. The DSU grant — diritto allo studio universitario — pays €7,000-plus a year in cash, waives tuition entirely, feeds you at the university canteen and puts a subsidized roof over your head. It is open to international students on exactly the same income rules as Italian students. The catch is administrative: there is no national application. Sixteen regional bodies run separate calls with separate deadlines, and for families living abroad the paperwork starts months before any portal opens.

What the DSU grant actually pays

For 2026/27 — the cycle whose calls have just closed — a student living away from home received at least €7,171.11 in cash and services per year, with the top band reaching €8,246.78 in several regions. Amounts are indexed annually, so expect the 2027/28 figures to rise slightly. The grant is need-based first: merit matters for keeping it, not for getting it.

[[chart:dsu-value]]
BenefitWhat it means in practice
Annual cash grant€7,171 to €8,247 for students living away from home (fuori sede), 2026/27 reference values, paid in instalments.
Tuition fee waiverWinners in good standing study tuition-free at public universities; only regional taxes and insurance remain.
Free canteen mealsA set number of subsidized (often free) meals per year at the university canteen.
Accommodation placeA subsidized residence bed — allocated first to fuori sede and international students, often with a further fee reduction.
Book allowance / servicesBudgets for study materials, plus access to sports and cultural services at reduced rates.

The income ceilings: ISEE and ISPE

Eligibility hangs on two numbers calculated from your family’s finances. The ISEE parificato (income-plus-assets index for households abroad) must sit below €28,339.88 at national level, and the ISPE (asset-only index) below €61,608.48 — though many regions set stricter limits, down to around €23,000 in Palermo. Three details trip up international families every single year:

  • Property is valued by formula, not market price — a flat €500 per square metre, so a 100 m² family home counts as €50,000 of assets whatever it is worth.
  • Documents must be issued by your home country’s authorities — household composition, every adult’s income, property records, and bank balances at 31 December — then apostilled (or consular-legalised) and translated into Italian. Self-declarations are refused.
  • Reference years differ by agency: some agencies assess foreign documents themselves using 2025 income for 2026/27; CAF-based procedures used 2024. Get this wrong and the ISEE comes out invalid.

The 2027/28 timeline

The 2026/27 application windows are closed, which makes now the right moment to prepare. Regional calls for 2027/28 are expected from June 2027, most closing between late August and late September — ER-GO’s first-year window, for example, shut on 24 August in 2026, well before enrolment was complete. Working backwards: gather and apostille family documents in spring 2027, obtain translations by early summer, apply to your programme as soon as its portal opens, and file the DSU application the week it opens. Provisional rankings arrive in October, final rankings by December; the grant is paid in instalments from late autumn.

One rule decides whether you keep the money: first-year students must earn roughly 20 CFU credits by 10 August of the following year. Miss it and the grant converts to a loan to repay.

Which regional body covers you

The agency is determined by where you enrol, never by where you come from. ER-GO covers Emilia-Romagna (Bologna, Parma, Ferrara); DSU Toscana covers Florence, Pisa and Siena; EDISU covers Piedmont (Turin); LazioDisco covers Rome; DiSCo covers Lombardy’s state universities alongside institutional schemes (Milan, Pavia); EDSU covers Sardinia (Cagliari, Sassari). Lombardy and Veneto add a wrinkle: several universities there run their own scholarship calls on top of the regional ones, with different deadlines. Identify your agency the day you shortlist a programme — every card in our database names it — because each body’s document rules and reference-year requirements differ in ways that decide whether your ISEE comes out valid.

Mistakes that cost the grant

  • Applying to the university but never to the agency. DSU is a separate application with its own, often earlier, deadline — the single most common loss.
  • Starting documents in June. Apostilles and consular legalisations take months in some countries; agencies refuse affidavits and self-declarations outright.
  • Using the wrong reference year. Agency-assessed procedures wanted 2025 income for 2026/27; CAF-based ones used 2024. Guessing invalidates the ISEE.
  • Assuming DSU counts as visa funds. It does not — consulates require separate proof of roughly €10,179.85 regardless of your application.

How DSU interacts with your visa

For the Italian type-D study visa, consulates require proof of roughly €10,179.85 per year from traceable sources — and explicitly, applying for DSU or being found eligible does not count towards that amount. Budget to show family funds for year one regardless of your application. Treat the DSU grant, once won, as the layer that makes everything after year one easy.

Because most Italian scholarship value concentrates on programmes with January-February admission rounds, many applicants pair DSU with Erasmus Mundus funding — our EMJM deadline calendar and Europe without IELTS guide cover both.
